words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) makes the ayah begin in continuation, not as a reset. Before the casting verb is heard, the reader is kept inside the earth sequence from 84:3, with the unstated feminine subject still recoverable. The connector allows additive coordination and a circumstantial feel within the larger suspended scene, but it does not sharpen the relation into a marked consequence the way a different result particle would. As a bound proclitic on {{ar:أَلْقَتْ}} ({{tr:ʾalqat}}), it also compresses connection and action into the first audible unit of the ayah.

words.prose: {{ar:أَلْقَتْ}} ({{tr:ʾalqat}}) is the first earth-predicate of the ayah: a perfect 3fs Form IV verb whose subject is the stretched earth carried over from 84:3, now active as discloser. Its direct object is {{ar:مَا فِيهَا}} ({{tr:mā fīhā}}), so the grammar turns the earth's hidden interior into something actively cast out, with no named recipient or landing-place. The root field of encounter is narrowed by the local form and object: this is not mutual meeting or arranged reception, but caused exposure, the earth making what was inside face the open. That same root later returns in {{ar:فَمُلَاقِيهِ}} ({{tr:fa-mulāqīhi}}) (84:6), so the casting already points toward meeting without collapsing the two uses. Inter-ayah contrasts sharpen the local action: a weight is cast upon the prophet in 73:5, and a staff is cast in 20:20, while here the earth casts out its own concealed load. The verb's sharp closure and its matched feminine perfect ending with {{ar:تَخَلَّتْ}} ({{tr:takhallat}}) make the two actions sound like paired stages of one release.

words.prose: {{ar:مَا}} ({{tr:mā}}) is the relative object head, not negation or a question. It keeps the object definite by construction yet unnamed in content: what is cast out is whatever was inside, not a specified class such as bodies, deposits, burdens, or records. The word cannot stand alone here; it opens a relative slot that {{ar:فِيهَا}} ({{tr:fīhā}}) completes, so containment defines the object. That differs from 99:2, where the earth's loads are named; 84:4 leaves the contents unnamed and lets interiority do the identifying.

words.prose: {{ar:فِيهَا}} ({{tr:fīhā}}) closes the relative object by saying where the cast-out thing was: inside the same feminine earth from 84:3. The preposition gives containment rather than possession, and the suffix packs location and earth-reference into one bound form at the point where the object is defined. This means the object is not generic hidden material but what belonged inside that earth's concealed domain. The phrase also keeps a concrete container image after the spreading of 84:3: the earth is not only a stretched surface; it still has an interior whose depth must be disclosed before {{ar:تَخَلَّتْ}} ({{tr:takhallat}}) names clearance.

words.prose: The second {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) arrives only after {{ar:مَا فِيهَا}} ({{tr:mā fīhā}}) has closed the object of {{ar:أَلْقَتْ}} ({{tr:ʾalqat}}). It enters as a bound connector on the fresh second predicate, {{ar:تَخَلَّتْ}} ({{tr:takhallat}}), over the same earth subject, so the ayah pivots from what the earth cast out to what the earth becomes without repeating the subject noun. Because the connector is {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}), not a sharper consequence particle, casting and emptying are paired closely without being reduced to a single mechanical result. Together the two connectors give the ayah an audible two-beat earth-release structure.

words.prose: {{ar:تَخَلَّتْ}} ({{tr:takhallat}}) is the closing predicate: another perfect 3fs verb over the same earth subject, but now without a direct object. After {{ar:أَلْقَتْ مَا فِيهَا}} ({{tr:ʾalqat mā fīhā}}), it moves attention from the expelled contents to the earth itself as the affected cleared domain, not to a new action performed on those contents. The root field gives vacancy, seclusion, and release pressure, while the local earth subject, the prior interior phrase, and the release sequence block a temporal elapsed sense. Form V makes that vacancy reflexive: the earth that was passively stretched in 84:3 is now portrayed as divesting itself, not merely being emptied by an outside evacuator or only stated to be empty. The omitted source complement stays recoverable from {{ar:مَا فِيهَا}} ({{tr:mā fīhā}}), which lets the last word land cleanly as cleared condition. Inter-ayah echoes add contrast without controlling the parse: a release command appears in 9:5, and private withdrawal appears in 2:14, while here the earth's own private interior is abolished. Qiraat boundary vocalization can keep the final feminine consonant audible in connection while preserving the same root, subject, and Form V analysis. The final position, doubled middle consonant, and feminine ending make the ayah close on compressed vacancy.

topics.reason: The verb is a 3fs perfect coordinated with the prior earth-predicate, and attachment evidence makes the subject syntactically controlled by the same earth referent.

topics.headline: objectless state-change

topics.reason: The final verb has no object in the local frame, so it names a state-change of the subject rather than a second transitive action on the contents.

topics.headline: source relation left unspoken

topics.reason: The bundle has no formal ellipsis entry, so the source complement is best kept as recoverable semantic compression from the prior object phrase rather than asserted as a syntactically supplied ellipsis.

topics.headline: vacancy with relinquishment
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final emptiness is relinquished interiority, not bare absence.
topics.reason: The broad root includes several branches, and local context selects vacancy, being clear, seclusion-turned-open, and relinquishment while not activating unrelated branches.

topics.blocking_evidence: The local earth subject, the prior phrase {{ar:فِيهَا}} ({{tr:fīhā}}), and the casting-clearance sequence select vacancy and relinquishment rather than elapsed time.
topics.reason: The row itself identifies the temporal branch as blocked; guardrail evidence agrees that the local frame is an intransitive state-change after casting out contents.

topics.reason: The seclusion branch is not the selected translation, but it gives a coherent contrast once the prior interior phrase has made hiddenness local.

topics.headline: Form V self-divestiture

topics.reason: The local form is Form V and intransitive, which supports self-directed state-change and excludes a causative evacuation frame as the local reading.

topics.reason: The final position, intransitive frame, Form V morphology, and preceding object phrase all support closure on cleared vacancy rather than a new object.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Casting out until no interior remainder exists.** `ل ق ي:B005` supplies casting or putting something down before another, and `خ ل و:B001` supplies being bare or empty. The verb order gives the mechanism directly: expulsion produces vacancy. I infer only the directional relation between the two supplied actions. The earth does not merely reveal some contents; it performs a complete transfer from interior to exposed surface.

2. **A liability discharged into the arena of meeting.** `خ ل و:B006` gives being clear of liability, while `ل ق ي:B004` gives face-to-face encounter and `ل ق ي:B007` what one meets of good or ill. The later human encounter and account (84:6–12) supply the judicial destination of what is cast out. The packet does not say the earth is legally liable; I infer that emptying clears its custody by delivering contents to encounter. *Takhallat* then reads as both material vacancy and release from custodial burden.

3. **The cast contents become cast-offs.** `ل ق ي:B006` supplies an abandoned or ownerless cast-off thing. Against the later books that reattach deeds to persons, the earth's casting momentarily removes burial and possession as protections. The packet gives disposal followed by personal records; I infer that what the earth disowns is subsequently reassigned by account. The ayah gains a stark intermediate image: hidden holdings are expelled before ownership is judicially restored.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The encounter in 84:6 and the books that follow turned the earth's casting into delivery to account. Most surprising was 84:23: once humans are also vessels that store, earth's emptying becomes a material preview of inward contents becoming knowable.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Casting as delivery into encounter.** **Lexical evidence:** fixed `أَلْقَتْ` activates `ل ق ي` B005, casting something down or before another; 84:6 uses the same root in `ملاقيه`, `ل ق ي` B004, two things coming face to face. `خ ل و` B001 supplies becoming empty. **Structural cue and role:** the earth casts what is inside, becomes empty, and two ayat later the human is told that the directed toil ends in encounter. **Abductive move:** the packet does not identify the expelled contents with what is met; I infer that the casting is a delivery operation that makes encounter possible. **Reading change:** the earth’s emptying becomes an active handoff into confrontation, not mere evacuation.

2. **A custodian clearing itself of liability.** **Lexical evidence:** `خ ل و` B006 is being clear of liability, while `ل ق ي` B005 supplies depositing or setting something before another. The nearby `كتاب` (`ك ت ب` B002/B003) and `حساب` (`ح س ب` B001) supply document and reckoning. **Structural cue and role:** held contents pass out before a record is issued and account begins (84:7–8). **Abductive move:** the legal-custodial direction is inferred: the packet gives release, document, and account, but does not state that the earth was liable for what it held. **Reading change:** `وتخلت` can mean that the earth completes custody by surrendering its contents and stands discharged of them.

3. **Release that reverses enclosure.** **Lexical evidence:** `خ ل و` B008 is letting go or setting free; `ل ق ي` B005 is casting out. **Structural cue and role:** `ما فيها` first defines contents by enclosure, then the two verbs successively expel and release them. **Abductive move:** I infer that the second verb is not redundant but removes any residual claim or restraint after the first physical casting. **Reading change:** the ayah describes a two-step emptying: contents are expelled, then the container relinquishes them completely.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 84:23 supplies the strongest later reversal: `و ع ي` B001/B002 shows humans inwardly storing after the earth has surrendered everything it stored. This corrects any idea that 84:4 ends concealment; disclosure moves the site of custody from the cosmic container to the human interior, where it remains known.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, yüzde ortaya çıkan ve yüzü ya da ağız köşesini eğrilten bir hastalığı açıkça tanımlar. Verilen dal çerçevesi hastalığı, etkilenen bölgeyi ve görünür sonucu birlikte korur.

concept_map.definition: Yüzde ortaya çıkarak yüzün veya ağız köşesinin eğrilmesine yol açan bir hastalıktır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi bir şeyi bulunduğu yerden atma veya bırakma hareketini çekirdek yapar. Sevginin birine yöneltilmesi ve çözülecek bir sözün birine sunulması, aynı yöneltme yapısının bağımlı kullanımlarıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal atma ve bir hedefe yöneltme eylemidir; atılmış nesnenin kalıcı adı veya karşılıklı buluşma değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Çıplak atma eylemi ile sevgi yöneltme ve çözülecek söz sunma gibi kalıba bağlı kullanımlar ayrı belirtilir.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi bulunduğu yerden atmak, bırakmak veya belirli bir alıcıya yöneltmektir. Sevgi yöneltme ve çözülmesi istenen bir sözü birine sunma, bu hareketin kalıplaşmış kullanımlarıdır.

facets.statement: Bir nesne bulunduğu yerden atılır, fırlatılır veya bırakılır.

Soyut kullanımlarda sevgi birine yöneltilir veya çözmesi için birine bilmece niteliğinde söz sunulur.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanıklıklar atma ve bırakma hareketinde birleşir. Toplu claim, bu hareketin bir alıcıya yönelmesini, sevgi aktarımını ve çözülmesi istenen sözün sunulmasını da kapsar.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi eylemi değil, atılmış veya terk edilmiş şeyi adlandırır. Bez parçası, değersiz görülen nesne ve sahibinin bilinmediği buluntu bu sonuç durumunun örnekleridir; eski ibadet giysisi ise özel bir kullanımdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal atma eyleminden sonra yerde kalan veya terk edilen nesneyle sınırlıdır; atma hareketinin kendisi değildir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Çıplak ad, atılmış ya da terk edilmiş şeyi gösterir; eski ibadet giysisi yalnız özel tamlamadaki örnektir.

facets.statement: Gönderge, atma veya bırakma eyleminin sonucunda terk edilmiş durumda bulunan nesnedir.

Eski bir ibadet uygulamasında kutsal yapının çevresinde dönen kişinin çıkarıp bıraktığı giysi özel bir örnektir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tanıklıklar atılmış veya terk edilmiş nesne anlamında birleşir; bez parçası, değersiz eşya, sahibi bilinmeyen buluntu ve çıkarılıp bırakılan ibadet giysisi bu kapsamda anılır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın kişi veya şey niteliğini verir ve belirli saldırı, ölüm ya da fiziksel boşluk örneklerini çekirdeğe eklemez.

concept_map.definition: Kendisini koruyacak biri bulunmadığı için başkasının göz dikebildiği ve kolayca zarar görebilecek ya da ele geçirilebilecek kişi veya şeydir.

facets.statement: Kişi veya şey bir koruyucudan yoksundur ve bu yüzden başkasının kolay hedefi olur.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Bildirilen anlam, koruyucusuz olma ile bundan doğan göz dikilme ve kolay hedef haline gelme sonucunu birlikte taşır.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Bu dal korumasız kişi veya şeyin durumudur; komşu dal bir kişiyi belirli olarak ölüm tehlikesine maruz bırakan ettirici eylemdir.
